chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, altogether, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from al-Zuhri, who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'If those between the East and the West were to die, I would not feel lonely as long as the Quran is with me.' And when he (peace be upon him) recited 'Master of the Day of Judgment', he would repeat it until he was on the verge of dying.

key_terms.مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ: Master of the Day of Judgment (Quran 1:4)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn say about the Quran's ability to relieve loneliness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Quran as the ultimate spiritual companion (khalil) for the believer, a concept central to Shia piety where the text serves as a living guide against existential solitude. The Imam’s intense repetition of 'Maliki yawm al-din' reflects the Shia emphasis on the Day of Judgment as a pivotal moment of accountability, linking daily devotion with eschatological hope and awe.
